answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a scarce deposit before transacting, and peers may demand proof the identity is unique. When behavioral correlation exposes duplicates, the entire bond is slashed, so a sybil farm must fund many separate deposits and forfeit them all. Like a lantern burning only while fueled, an identity works only while capital is at risk; the garden of fake accounts becomes costly to seed, and the pigment of each reputation is a bond that vanishes on fraud. Attack cost scales linearly with identities; honest agents reclaim their stake.
